character_sheet: The Emperor Scorpion is a giant hostile scorpion: a wide flat head with two eyes and two hinged mandibles, an eight-segment body, two claw arms of four segments each ending in a pincer, eight five-segment legs (four a side) and an eight-segment tail curling up over the back to a three-piece stinger (EmperorScorpionModel.createBodyLayer, EmperorScorpionModel.java:182-576). It has 350 HP, 35 attack and 20 armour (createAttributes, EntityEmperorScorpion.java:108-115), fights on a bug melee goal whose hit poisons one time in three for 90 ticks (EmperorScorpionPoisonGoal at :96, EmperorScorpionPoisonGoal.java:18-32), and its strike throws the victim three blocks back (doHurtTarget :167-179). Every fourth tick it scans for prey (customServerAiStep :220-226, selectTarget :257-275) and, while it has a target, a 1-in-20 roll drops a baby Scorpion at the midpoint between them (:223-224, spawnBabyScorpionToward :230-243); it avenges hits (:100-101), ignores further damage for 30 ticks after each one (hurt :182-198), hops with a boost (jumpFromGround :158-164) and heals 2 on a rare roll (:206-209). It spawns at night in the dark above y 50 with air above it and no other Emperor within 20 blocks (checkSpawnRules :353-371), in badlands (the hostile_emperor_scorpion biome modifiers). Read it as a heavy armoured crawler: the legs plant one after another, the claws threaten, the tail arcs.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.5 of the rig (EmperorScorpionRenderer.java:27, applied :34-37; shadow 0.95 x 1.5) on a 256x128 sheet (EmperorScorpionModel.java:576); 3.5 x 3.0 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:241-243). The legs, claws and tail are chains the code positions segment by segment (an FK chain in code, design section 5: they become real parent-child bones in the converted rig) — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.axis: y (the sweep) and z (the lift on segments 2 and 3), with positions along the chain
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.12 = 0.377 rad (22 deg) x the walking speed, no threshold; the four leg pairs (1 and 5, 2 and 6, 3 and 7, 4 and 8) a quarter period apart, the right legs the negative; on the rising half-wave a lift of 0.47 x speed minus the sweep's magnitude, segment 2 about its −0.929 rad rest and segment 3 about +0.632 rad (mirrored on the right)
groups.plain: the eight legs sweep about the vertical with the stride in four phases a quarter period apart, each leg lifting as it swings forward; every segment from the second out yaws with the sweep and the knee, shin and foot are re-positioned along it (an FK chain in code)
groups.math: a_k = cos(t * 2.0 * 0.22 - k * pi/2) * pi * 0.12 * amount (k = 0..3 for legs 1/5, 2/6, 3/7, 4/8); left LegNSeg2..5.yRot = a_k; right LegNSeg2..4.yRot = -a_k, right LegNSeg5.yRot = a_k; lift = (a_k rising) ? 0.47 * amount - |a_k| : 0; left Seg2.zRot = -lift - 0.929, Seg3.zRot = -lift + 0.632 (right: +lift + 0.929, +lift - 0.632); Seg3/4/5 x,z from sin(a_k) x 6 / 9 / 1, y from sin of the lifts x 11.5
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 2.0 x wingspeed 0.22 = 0.44 rad/tick: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.44 = 14.28 ticks; the lift test compares the wave one tenth of a tick ahead (:586, :588)

groups.name: mandibles
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.05 = 0.157 rad (9 deg) at rest (0.5 x 0.22 = 0.11 rad/tick); pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg) attacking (2.5 x 0.22 = 0.55 rad/tick); the right tip the negative of the left
groups.plain: the two mandible tips scissor slowly at rest and snap fast and wide while the attacking flag is set
groups.math: a = attacking == 0 ? cos(t * 0.5 * 0.22) * pi * 0.05 : cos(t * 2.5 * 0.22) * pi * 0.15; LeftManPart2.zRot = a; RightManPart2.zRot = -a
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (EntityEmperorScorpion.java:48, set by the melee goal's IntConsumer at :96) selects the rhythm
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.5 x wingspeed 0.22 = 0.11 rad/tick at rest (period 57.1 ticks); attacking 2.5 x 0.22 = 0.55 (period 11.4 ticks)

groups.name: claws_tail
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg): a moving claw swings its upper segment by it about ∓1.57, turns its fixed finger by it about ±0.074 and closes its pincer finger by its negative about ±0.371 (forearm, palm and pincer re-positioned along the swing); the moving tail flexes segments 1-3 by +a about their rest bends (0.594, +0.484, +0.632), segments 4-5 by −a, segment 6 by −1.5 a, segment 7 by −2.5 a, the stinger pieces by +0.66 a / +a / +1.7 a, each segment placed at the end of the one before
groups.plain: the claws and the tail share one wave but each moves only in the periods a per-entity random latch picks for it: at rest each claw in two periods of twenty and the tail in one of twenty-five, attacking each claw in two of four and the tail in one of three; a part not picked holds its rest pose
groups.math: a = cos(t * 3.0 * 0.22) * pi * 0.15; at each rising zero-crossing ri1 = attacking ? nextInt(4) : nextInt(20), ri2 = attacking ? nextInt(3) : nextInt(25); doLeftClaw(ri1 in {1,3} ? a : 0); doRightClaw(ri1 in {2,3} ? a : 0); doTail(ri2 == 1 ? a : 0)
groups.phase: a per-entity random latch (RenderInfo ri1 / ri2, re-rolled at each rising zero-crossing of the wave: :626-635) selects which of the three chains move this period; the attacking flag loads the dice
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 3.0 x wingspeed 0.22 = 0.66 rad/tick: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.66 = 9.52 ticks; the zero-crossing test compares the wave one tenth of a tick ahead (:625)

behaviour: Three rhythms. The eight legs walk on one speed-scaled wave at 0.44 rad/tick (a 14.3-tick stride) in four phases a quarter period apart: every leg segment from the second out yaws with the sweep, the knee, shin and foot are re-positioned along it by sine (an FK chain in code), and the leg lifts on its forward half-wave by 0.47 x speed less the sweep's magnitude (EmperorScorpionModel.java:585-616, :735-769). Standing still the legs rest.

The two mandible tips scissor about z at 0.11 rad/tick and 9 degrees at rest, 0.55 rad/tick and 27 degrees while the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte is set (:617-619; the byte is EntityEmperorScorpion.java:48, set by the melee goal's IntConsumer registered at :96).

The claws and the tail share one 0.66 rad/tick wave (a 9.5-tick period) but each moves only when a per-entity random latch picks it at the start of a period: at rest each claw moves in 2 periods of 20 and the tail in 1 of 25; attacking each claw in 2 of 4 and the tail in 1 of 3 (:624-650). A moving claw swings its upper segment 27 degrees and closes its pincer finger against the swing; the moving tail flexes every segment about its rest bend and the stinger curls with it (:771-823).
The head, the eyes, the body segments, the shoulders, the mandible bases and the legs' hip roots are static; the head does not track the look angle and the walk position plays no part.

The strike is the melee goal's (EmperorScorpionPoisonGoal, a BugMeleeAttackGoal, EntityEmperorScorpion.java:96) and its poison lands on the hit; the baby-scorpion summon (:223-224) and the 30-tick invulnerability after a hit (:183-185) are timed by the AI, not by animation events.

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 EmperorScorpionModel row (geckolib_migration_design.md:441): 'Head [0.9,0.7] @1; Seg4 [1.4,0.8] @0.5; LeftPincer/RightPincer [0.65,0.5] @0.5; Leg1Seg1…Leg8Seg5 [0.22,0.45] @0.5; Tailseg1/Tailseg4/Tailseg8 [0.35,0.45] @0.25; Stinger3 [0.4,0.4] @1'. Every design name resolves to the port model's part names as written (EmperorScorpionModel.createBodyLayer); the leg family Leg1Seg1…Leg8Seg5 is listed member by member (40 bones). The row writes the main size as [1.5,1.5]; the registration is 3.5 x 3.0 (ModEntities.java:241-243) — the profile takes the registered size (the shared laws), which the owner reconciles.
formulas: `EmperorScorpionModel.poseFrom` (EmperorScorpionModel.java:588-659, with the helpers doLeftLeg :743-759, doRightLeg :761-777, doLeftClaw :779-787, doRightClaw :789-797 and doTail :799-831; orig ModelEmperorScorpion.java:569-720 in `render` (func_78088_a, with its helpers at :732-820; func_78087_a at :728-730 is a bare super call), wingspeed 0.22 from `new ModelEmperorScorpion(0.22f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:426 - the port's WINGSPEED): four leg pairs walk a quarter turn apart - for pair k (0 to 3) the swing is the cosine of the age in ticks times 2.0 times the wingspeed, less k times 1.570795, times pi, times 0.12, times the walking speed, and a lift of 0.47 times the walking speed less the absolute swing applies when the same cosine 0.1 ticks later is larger (the leg rising); the left leg of the pair (legs 1 to 4) takes the swing, the right leg (5 to 8) its negative. Down each leg the four outer segments yaw by the swing (the right leg's fifth segment by its negative); the second segment rolls by minus the lift minus 0.929 and the third by minus the lift plus 0.632 (the right leg the negatives); the third segment sits 6 units behind the second along the sine of the yaw and 6 minus 6 times the absolute sine to the side, the fourth 9 and 9 further, the fifth 1 and 1, each dropping 11.5 times the sine of the roll above it and the fifth 6.5 units lower (the right leg mirrored in x and y, in double arithmetic). The mandibles roll by the cosine of the age times 0.5 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.05 at rest, or times 2.5 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.15 attacking (the right one the negative). When the cosine of the age times 3.0 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.15 crosses zero rising (a look-ahead of 0.1 ticks) the entity's random re-rolls the selectors: at rest ri1 from 20 and ri2 from 25, attacking from 4 and 3. The left claw poses on that wave when ri1 is 1 or 3 (else on 0): the first arm segment yaws by -1.57 plus the angle, the second segment sits at z = -22 less 12 times the cosine of that yaw and the third, fourth segments and the pincer 11 less again (x and y the bind), the third segment yaws by 0.074 plus the angle and the pincer by 0.371 minus it; the right claw mirrors it when ri1 is 2 or 3 (1.57 minus the angle, -0.074 minus, -0.371 plus). The tail poses on the wave when ri2 is 1 (else on 0): the first segment pitches by 0.594 plus the angle and each further segment by the previous pitch plus its own step - 0.484 plus the angle, 0.632 plus, 0.557 minus, 0.632 minus, -5.501 minus three halves of the angle minus 0.4, -2.822 minus two and a half times the angle minus 2.2, the eighth as the seventh - each sitting 9 units (the second) or 10 units (the third to seventh) from the previous segment's pivot along the negative sine (y) and cosine (z) of the previous pitch, the eighth at the seventh's place; the three stinger pieces continue at 10, 3 and 3 units with pitches of the seventh's plus 0.66 times the angle, then minus 0.48 plus the angle, then minus 1.01 plus 1.7 times the angle (x the bind throughout). The look yaw, look pitch and walk position play no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (EmperorScorpionGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations: the statements write a FlatRig, the classic flat rig, and FlatRig.resolve maps it onto the shipped hierarchy - a chain child's local rotation and position are those that reproduce the classic world transform above).
